answer: Beacon-chained age proofs: each identity roots its chain in a walnut, one sealed seed answer hashed at enrollment, then every epoch appends a link hashing the prior link with that epoch's signed beacon, unknowable in advance. History cannot be backfilled, so k links cost k real epochs of liveness: fresh clones carry no weight and accrue glacier-slow while paying k machines per round. A nightly mirror audit re-walks every tip against the beacon log; one forked chain shared by two identities slashes both, making pooled clones strictly worse than one honest chain.
